messages:
jay: noticing a repeated NVMe I/O & temp burst in ap-south1, some GPU pods stuck attaching
meera: saw the alert at 04:12 UTC, which pool?
jay: pool=ephemeral-hot-5, hosts gnode-apse1-301..307. dmesg snippet: 
jay: ```
[ 45234.101010] nvme2n1: I/O error, status 0x2
[ 45234.101500] nvme2n1: media_error LBA 0x1c20-0x1c80
[ 45234.102000] nvme2n1: temperature above threshold: 79C
```
tonY: that temp is scary. smartctl shows rising reallocated sectors on 302 and 305
meera: timeline: spike began right after we rolled vendor firmware v3.4.1 during the midnight window
irene: any sign of data corruption or only kernel errors?
jay: kernel reassign + I/O errors only, no S3-level corruption reports yet
meera: internal hypothesis: FW changed GC timing so small high-frequency trims are executing more aggressively -> write amp and thermal cycles
tonY: immediate mitigations: 1) cordon hosts from gpu-service 2) throttle janitor/trim frequency 3) apply kernel nvme_trim_aggressive=0 on a canary
irene: cordon sounds lowest-risk. shifting load will increase costs elsewhere though
jay: cordoning gnode-301..307 now, running drain --grace 300. ETA ~9m
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-APSE-NVME-THERM-2026 responders=[jay, meera, tony, irene]
tonY: also propose running fio small-write sim on gnode-304 as a canary instead of fleet rollback
meera: fio command: fio --name=4krand --rw=randwrite --bs=4k --iodepth=32 --numjobs=8 --size=8G
jay: running canary fio on 304 after drain completes
irene: vendor already paged; asked to halt rollouts and provide firmware diff focusing on TRIM/GC scheduling
tonY: cost estimate if we move batch launches off ap-south1: ~+$1k/day in spot premium + potential egress if data moves
meera: applied janitor cadence change for ephemeral-hot-5: 20m -> 60m and enabled backlog alert at 40%
ops-bot: Update INC-APSE-NVME-THERM-2026 status=investigating
jay: drain complete for 7 hosts, attach fail rate dropped from ~14% -> 2.1% in 22m
meera: canary fio + kernel toggle on 304: temp p95 dropped from 78C -> 68C during same workload; write_amp metric down ~45%
tonY: no user-facing errors reported, kernel I/O stays the only signal so far
irene: vendor response: release notes show TRIM scheduler tweak; they've paused rollout and are gathering reproduction logs
jay: ops follow-up: 1) keep hosts cordoned until vendor reply 2) keep janitor cadence doubled 3) keep canary under 12h observation 4) open procurement ticket for drive lifecycle and RMA policy
ops-bot: Incident INC-APSE-NVME-THERM-2026 updated: status=mitigated
meera: scheduling postmortem tomorrow 11:00 UTC; include firmware diff, janitor change history, and potential long-term policy (canary firmware window)
tonY: ack. will upload perf charts (nvme_temp, write_amp_ratio, attach_fail_pct, janitor_ops/s)
irene: closing realtime ops. leave thread for postmortem notes
jay: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
